definitions.explanation: Designated seats on trains and buses for elderly, pregnant, disabled, or injured passengers.

examples.japanese: {優先席|ゆうせんせき}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦お{年寄|としよ}り→年寄り：03460_toshiyori⟧⟦や→や：10080_ya⟧⟦{妊婦|にんぷ}→妊婦：20357_ninpu⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦ため→ため：01145_tame⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦ある→ある：00006_aru⟧。
examples.english: Priority seats are for elderly and pregnant passengers.

examples.japanese: {優先席|ゆうせんせき}⟦{付近|ふきん}→付近：00044_fukin⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{携帯電話|けいたいでんわ}→携帯電話：04433_keitaidenwa⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{電源|でんげん}→電源：04429_dengen⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦お{切|き}り→切る：02693_kiru⟧⟦ください→ください：02899_kudasai⟧。
examples.english: Please turn off your mobile phone near the priority seats.

examples.japanese: {優先席|ゆうせんせき}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{座|すわ}っていたら→座る：00757_suwaru⟧、⟦お{年寄|としよ}り→年寄り：03460_toshiyori⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{来|き}た→来る：00254_kuru⟧⟦ので→ので：09501_node⟧⟦{席|せき}→席：02215_seki⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{譲|ゆず}った→譲る：02323_yuzuru⟧。
examples.english: I was sitting in the priority seat, but an elderly person came so I gave up my seat.

notes:
USAGE: {優先席|ゆうせんせき} are found on most trains, buses, and subways in Japan. While anyone may sit there when empty, passengers are expected to give up the seat to those who need it.

WHO SHOULD USE:
・⟦{高齢者|こうれいしゃ}→高齢者：15649_koureisha⟧/⟦お{年寄|としよ}り→年寄り：03460_toshiyori⟧ (elderly)
・⟦{妊婦|にんぷ}→妊婦：20357_ninpu⟧ (pregnant women)
・⟦{障害者|しょうがいしゃ}→障害者：27165_shougaisha⟧ (people with disabilities)
・⟦{怪我人|けがにん}→怪我人：23513_keganin⟧ (injured people)
・⟦{乳幼児|にゅうようじ}→乳幼児：14882_nyuuyouji⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{連|つ}れた→連れる：01240_tsureru⟧⟦{方|かた}→方：10665_kata⟧ (people with small children)

MOBILE PHONE ETIQUETTE: Signs often request that phones be set to silent mode or turned off near {優先席|ゆうせんせき} due to concerns about pacemaker interference, though this rule has been relaxed in many areas.

SIMILAR TERMS:
・⟦シルバーシート→シルバーシート：29367_shirubaashiito⟧ (silver seat - older term for priority seat)
